description: The agent must: (1) Detect that the `open-agreements` CLI is available locally by running `command -v open-agreements` or equivalent. (2) Run `open-agreements list --json` to discover available NDA templates and their exact field definitions — it MUST pick the `common-paper-one-way-nda` template (not a mutual NDA), as the business context specifies one-directional disclosure. (3) Parse the field definitions from the list output to determine the exact field names required by the one-way NDA template (e.g., `disclosing_party_name`, `receiving_party_name`, `effective_date`, `purpose` — exact names vary and must be read from CLI output). (4) Write a correctly structured JSON file to `/tmp/oa-values.json` with NovaBiotek Inc. as disclosing party, Genomatix CRO Ltd. as receiving party, July 1, 2025 as effective date, and the clinical trial evaluation purpose. (5) Run `open-agreements fill common-paper-one-way-nda -d /tmp/oa-values.json -o /workspace/legal/contracts/genomatix_one_way_nda.docx` to generate the DOCX. (6) Clean up by running `rm /tmp/oa-values.json`. The proprietary trap is the exact CLI flag syntax (`-d` for data file, `-o` for output), the exact template name (`common-paper-one-way-nda`), and the exact field names which can only be discovered by calling the CLI's list command — a generic agent would guess wrong field names or use a mutual NDA template.
